name: Plug-in busway
summary: Busway with tap-off outlets along its length, drawn with outlet marks where plug-in units can be connected.
description: Plug-in busway distributes power along its route through outlets into which tap-off units can be inserted. It is common in rising mains in multi-storey buildings, factory floors and data halls, where loads change and new feeders are added without rewiring.

The symbol shows that outlets exist but not which are used. Tap-off units actually fitted are drawn separately with their protective devices. Readers should not assume every outlet mark represents a connected load, and voltage drop calculations should use the actual tap-off positions.
readingNotes: Distinguish outlet positions from fitted tap-off units.
Check voltage drop to the most remote tap-off.
drawingChecklist: Mark outlet positions on the layout.
distinction: Plug-in busway has outlets for tap-off units; feeder busway carries power point to point only.
